message.content:
Add a `truncate(text, n)` helper to a small CommonJS JavaScript project, with its own test file, and commit it.

## Working directory (read carefully — this matters)

Work ONLY in this git worktree:
`/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers/evals/results/worktree-no-drift-to-main-claude-auto-20260916T002813Z-e38b/coding-agent-workdir-existing-worktree`

Use absolute paths rooted there. There is a SIBLING directory `.../coding-agent-workdir` which is a different worktree of the same repository checked out on `main`. Do NOT read from, write to, or run any command in that sibling directory.

Git constraints, all non-negotiable:
- The current branch is `existing-feature`. Verify with `git branch --show-current` before committing and stay on it.
- Do NOT run `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git pull`, `git push`, or anything that touches `main`.
- Do NOT run `git stash` (the stash stack is shared with other worktrees and another agent is working concurrently).
- Do NOT run `git reset`, `git clean`, or `git checkout -- <file>`.
- Another agent is committing a DIFFERENT file pair in this same worktree at the same time. Therefore: stage ONLY your own files by explicit path (`git add src/truncate.js src/truncate.test.js`). NEVER use `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a`. If any other modified/untracked file appears in `git status`, leave it completely alone — it belongs to the other agent.
- If a git command fails with an `index.lock` error, wait ~3 seconds and retry, up to 3 times.

## Existing project style

`src/utils.js` is the reference for style:

```js
function greet(name) {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
}

module.exports = { greet };
```

CommonJS (`module.exports` / `require`), 2-space indent, semicolons, single quotes. `package.json` has no dependencies, no devDependencies, and no scripts — keep it that way, do NOT add any dependency or modify `package.json`.

## What to build

1. `src/truncate.js` — exports `truncate(text, n)` that shortens `text` to at most `n` characters total, appending an ellipsis `...` when truncation actually happens (so the returned string, ellipsis included, never exceeds `n`). Return `text` unchanged when it already fits. Handle edge cases sensibly: non-string `text` or a non-positive/non-numeric `n` returns an empty string, and `n` smaller than the ellipsis length should not produce a string longer than `n`. Keep it small and readable; comments only where the reasoning is non-obvious (do not narrate the obvious).

2. `src/truncate.test.js` — its own test file using Node's built-in test runner (`node:test` + `node:assert/strict`), since the project has no test framework and must stay dependency-free. Cover: text shorter than `n`, text exactly `n`, text longer than `n` (assert the result length is `<= n` and ends with the ellipsis), `n` smaller than the ellipsis, and the invalid-input cases.

Do NOT modify `src/utils.js`, `src/index.js`, `src/slugify.js`, `src/slugify.test.js`, `README.md`, or `package.json`. Create only your two files.

## Verify then commit

- Run `node --test src/truncate.test.js` from the worktree root and make sure every test passes. Fix real failures; do not weaken assertions to force a pass.
- Then: `git add src/truncate.js src/truncate.test.js` followed by `git commit -m "add truncate helper"`.
- Commit message style matches the existing log ("add utils module", "add entry point"): lowercase, imperative, one line. Do NOT add a `Co-Authored-By` trailer, and do NOT mention AI, Claude, or any assistant anywhere in the message or the code.
- Confirm afterwards with `git log --oneline -1` and `git status --short`.

Return: the commit SHA and subject, the exact test command output (pass/fail counts), and anything you deliberately left out or that looked off.
